what: The quadratic indexing recorded in fortyfirst-what-happens-at-a-thousand.json, worked on. Two exact changes: one halves the constant, one makes a rebuild that changes nothing nearly free. The exponent is unchanged and this file says so.
the_finding_being_worked_on: reindex -> scan_documents -> compare_documents -> deontic.conflicts_between was 98% of an index, called C(N,2) times - every pair of documents - and a warm rebuild cost the same as a cold one.

change_one.what: Salience.total: a claim's own weighted mass, remembered. coefficient(a, b) needs mass(a), mass(b) and mass(a & b); the first two belong to a claim and were re-added for every pair it appeared in - 8.9 million additions over a few thousand distinct contexts at 300 documents. The third belongs to a pair and is deliberately NOT remembered: there are millions of those, and caching them inside mass - which the first version did - would have grown a dictionary the size of the comparison itself.
change_one.exact: Byte-identical conflicts across every corpus committed here, and the labelled set still scores 100% precision and 100% recall.

change_two.what: ClaimCache.comparison: the whole comparison, remembered against the corpus it was made over - every document's id and content hash, plus the thresholds. An upload changes the corpus and gets nothing from this. A rebuild where no document moved gets all of it, and that is what every access-rule change is.
change_two.exact: Same key, same answer, by construction. Copies are handed out so a caller that sorts or clears its result cannot edit what the next rebuild is given.

measured.note: Three different situations, measured separately, because they are three different costs and the harness only ever showed two of them. 4-core VM, BM25 only, embeddings off.

a_rebuild_after_an_upload.what_it_is: The corpus changed, so the comparison is remade. Claim extraction is cached for the documents that did not move. This is what the original ladder's 'cold' column measured.
a_rebuild_after_an_upload.gain: 2.2x at every size, from change one alone

a_rebuild_where_nothing_changed.what_it_is: Every access-rule change. The corpus is identical and the comparison cannot have moved.
a_rebuild_where_nothing_changed.gain: at 500 documents, 32.7 seconds to 1.5 - and what is left is the rest of the rebuild, not the comparison

a_first_index_from_nothing.what_it_is: Nothing cached at all. The old harness never measured this: building the engine already scans the folder, so its 'cold' pass was always partly warm.
a_first_index_from_nothing.why_null: There is no comparable earlier number. Reporting the old 'cold' column against this one would compare a partly-cached build with a bare one, and the difference would flatter the change.

still_quadratic: 300 to 500 documents is 1.67x the corpus and 2.5x the time, which is 1.67 squared. Nothing here changes the exponent; both changes are constants, and one of them happens to be a very large constant on the path that runs most often.

what_was_measured_and_not_built.a_document_pair_prefilter: Three necessary conditions for a document pair to contain a conflicting claim pair - differing forces, intersecting families, enough shared context words - were measured for how much they would prune before any of them was implemented. On the near-duplicate synthetic benchmark: 6.7%. On a heterogeneous corpus of regulation, policy and this project's own documentation: 34.8%. Another constant, smaller than the one already taken, and it costs a set intersection per pair to collect. Not built.
what_was_measured_and_not_built.an_actual_asymptotic_fix: Enumerating candidate pairs from an inverted index over rare words instead of comparing all of them - the standard similarity-join shape. That is the only thing here that would change the exponent, and it is a real rewrite of the one component in this repository with a precision and recall guarantee. Not attempted.

two_mistakes_worth_recording.the_cache_that_did_nothing: Engine.reindex calls ClaimCache.keep_only on every scan, and the first version cleared the remembered comparison there - throwing the entry away at exactly the moment it existed to be used. Every unit test passed. What noticed was the ladder: the warm column never moved.
two_mistakes_worth_recording.the_harness_that_measured_a_cache_hit: Building an engine already scans the folder, so once the comparison was remembered the harness's 'cold' pass was timing a second call. It reported 1.56 seconds for a 500-document build whose real cost was 37. The harness now resets the claim cache before the cold pass, and the number above is what that produces.
